title: Zero forcing in the regular 4-polytopes
statement: Colour a set Z of vertices black; whenever a black vertex has exactly one white neighbour, that neighbour turns black. Z is a zero forcing set when this turns every vertex black, and the zero forcing number Z(G) is the smallest size of a zero forcing set. Determine Z(G) for the graphs of the six regular convex 4-polytopes (the 5-cell K5; the tesseract, 16 vertices; the 16-cell, 8 vertices; the 24-cell, 24 vertices, 8-regular; the 600-cell, 120 vertices, 12-regular; the 120-cell, 600 vertices, 4-regular) and of the two E8 polytopes 3_21 (Gosset, 56 vertices, 27-regular) and 4_21 (the 240 roots of E8, 56-regular), each vertex adjacent to its nearest neighbours. First values (ours): the 5-cell 4 (exact); the tesseract (8-cell) 8 (exact); the 16-cell 6 (exact); the 24-cell 14; the 600-cell 44; the 120-cell 106; the Gosset polytope 3_21 44; the E8 root polytope 4_21 182. The headline cell is the 120-cell: find a certificate with value 105 or less (the largest multiplicity of an adjacency eigenvalue (Z >= M >= that multiplicity): >= 48 for the 120-cell), or prove 106 optimal.
submission: Text file: the vertex numbers of the set (spaces or newlines), in the checker's vertex order (the 120-cell).
score: the number of vertices in the set (smaller is better)

best_known.source: Quantavane (Arhan Canli), 10 November 2026: 106 for the 120-cell, best found: CP-SAT (one worker, 5 to 60 seconds) on the model of tools/polytope_sets.py, or, for zero forcing and power domination, greedy completion and pruning between rounds of fort cuts

context: Zero forcing was introduced by the AIM Minimum Rank-Special Graphs Work Group (2008) as an upper bound for the maximum nullity M(G) of the real symmetric matrices whose off-diagonal pattern is the graph, and independently in the control of quantum systems (Burgarth and Giovannetti 2007); computing it is NP-hard. Since A - tI has the graph's pattern for every eigenvalue t of the adjacency matrix A, Z(G) >= M(G) >= the largest eigenvalue multiplicity, a strong bound for these vertex-transitive graphs with highly degenerate spectra: 36 for the 600-cell, 48 for the 120-cell, 27 for 3_21 and 112 for 4_21. For the hypercubes Z(Q_n) = M(Q_n) = 2^(n-1) (AIM 2008), so the tesseract cell is known; for the other polytopes the question is how close Z comes to the spectral bound, i.e. whether the minimum rank of these graphs is attained by their adjacency matrices.
references: AIM Minimum Rank-Special Graphs Work Group, Zero forcing sets and the minimum rank of graphs, Linear Algebra Appl. 428 (2008) 1628-1648
D. Burgarth, V. Giovannetti, Full control by locally induced relaxation, Phys. Rev. Lett. 99 (2007) 100501
B. Brimkov, C. C. Fast, I. V. Hicks, Computational approaches for zero forcing and related problems, European J. Oper. Res. (2019)
H. S. M. Coxeter, Regular Polytopes (3rd ed., Dover 1973)

novelty.verdict: new. No zero forcing result for the 600-cell, the 120-cell, the 24-cell or the E8 polytopes (searched with E8 and Gosset) was found on arXiv, in the journal literature (Crossref) or by web search; the known values for hypercubes and complete graphs cover only the small cells.
closest: General results on zero forcing (the references) and its values for hypercubes, grids and products; none for these polytopes.
Our polytope problems (polytope-ising, potts3-600, cell600-idcode, cell600-forest, cell120-coil, e8-idcode, e8-resolving): other invariants of the same graphs.
